name: Daniel Joseph Houston
current_role: Retired Executive Chair of Principal Financial Group (2025); director of ADT Inc. and Arch Capital Group; co-chair, ICON Water Trail board
profile: Dan Houston joined Bankers Life (later Principal Financial Group) in 1984 straight out of Iowa State, selling the then-new 401(k), and rose to CEO in 2015 and chairman in 2016. He retired in 2025 after a 41-year career and now sits on the ADT and Arch Capital boards while focusing on Des Moines civic projects such as the ICON Water Trail.
interesting_fact: He spent his entire 41-year career at one company, starting as a young recruit hired to sell the brand-new 401(k) product and finishing as chairman and CEO of Principal.
deep_cut_fact: A vintage-car enthusiast, he owns 1961 and 1963 Corvettes and a 1970 Mustang, but his favourite is a 1970 El Camino Super Sport; as a teen he raised pigs on his grandparents' farm near Dow City, Iowa, earning about $5,000 one summer.
notes: Now retired from Principal; best routes are via his board roles or Des Moines civic organisations (ICON Water Trail, Community Foundation of Greater Des Moines). No personal published contact found. Strong fit for an entrepreneurship/infrastructure angle (water trail, public transit).

name: Barry Hytinen
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Iron Mountain Inc.; director, ABM Industries
profile: Barry Hytinen has been CFO of Iron Mountain since January 2020, helping steer the records-storage company's push into data centers. Before that he was CFO of Hanesbrands and spent 12 years at Tempur Sealy (including as CFO), after earlier finance roles at GE, Vignette and venture-backed Fogbreak Software.
interesting_fact: As CFO he is a key financial architect of Iron Mountain's pivot from paper-records storage into a fast-growing data-center business, highly relevant to a data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He is a 1997 political science graduate of Syracuse University's Maxwell School (later Harvard MBA), and early on was VP Finance at Fogbreak Software, a small venture-backed Milpitas software startup.
notes: Fogbreak detail comes from secondary bio aggregators (marketscreener/vectorshift); Syracuse/Harvard and Tempur/Hanes facts are from the Maxwell page. Route via Iron Mountain IR or media team.

name: Joshua J. Ofman
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, GRAIL, Inc. (multi-cancer early detection; Galleri test)
profile: Josh Ofman, MD, MSHS, is CEO of GRAIL, maker of the Galleri multi-cancer early-detection blood test, having joined in 2019 and served as Chief Medical Officer and President. Before GRAIL he spent 15+ years at Amgen, finishing as SVP Global Value, Access and Policy. In 2026 he led Galleri through its FDA premarket review, which won a favourable advisory-panel vote in September.

name: Jason Trevisan
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, CarGurus, Inc.

Before CarGurus he spent about 12 years at venture firm Polaris Partners (General Partner from 2010), and earlier worked at aQuantive and Bain & Company.

current_role: Private investor; 10%-plus holder of ProFrac Holding Corp. (via the Wilks family); trustee, The Thirteen Foundation (Cisco, Texas)

The family's philanthropy/political giving is politically sensitive; approach via ProFrac (energy/fracking angle) if at all. The $50M figure comes from DeSmog; ProPublica confirms the trustee roles.

name: James V Continenza
current_role: Executive Chairman (since Feb 2019) and Chief Executive Officer (since July 2020), Eastman Kodak Company
profile: Jim Continenza is a turnaround specialist who joined Kodak's board in 2013, became Executive Chairman in 2019 and CEO in 2020, refocusing the company on print, advanced materials and chemicals. His earlier career was in telecom: AT&T, Lucent Technologies Product Finance, Teligent and STi Prepaid, and he has chaired marketing-tech firm Vivial since 2012.

deep_cut_fact: He started his career at AT&T, where he worked until 1997, and he holds a liberal arts bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin.
notes: Kodak press releases list individual media staff emails that vary by release; check the latest release for the current media contact. Kodak's advanced materials/battery-component work could be an energy angle.
